newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Oil to cut distribution costs.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Oil to cut distribution costs.

text.p: Japanese refiner Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd said on Tuesday it plans to cut costs by 300 million yen annually by rationalising distribution of lubricant oil.
A company spokesman said the firm would reduce the number of its lubricant oil and fuel oil tanks in the country to 23 from 43 by April 1998.
Information on inventory levels would be computerised and orders automated, he said.
Joint distribution of oil products with other refiners could be a future option, the spokesman added.
Japanese refiners have suffered sharp falls in their earnings in the first half of the current business year.

This is because costs have surged due to rising global crude prices and a weaker yen against the dollar, while domestic oil product prices remain poor due to tough competition at gasoline stations and consumers' opposition to a rise in prices.
Earlier this month, Mitsubishi Oil said its parent current profit for the six months to September 30 dropped 73.1 percent from the same period a year earlier, to 2.57 billion yen.
